end.summary:
Observed an example of a plant bending toward a window.
Practised distinguishing observation, hypothesis, law and theory; the distinction was not steady yet and needs checking next time.
The scientific meaning of “theory” versus everyday use was shown with a new-situation example.
Practised how evidence can support or overturn an idea; this needs further checking.
Theories-versus-laws mix-up appeared again at the end and was not corrected after its last occurrence.
end.parentNote: Asha practised the meanings of observation, hypothesis, law and theory using examples and follow-up questions. Tara used the scientific meaning of theory correctly in a new-situation example, including that theories explain why while laws describe patterns. The mix-up that theories become laws, and that laws are higher, appeared again at the end, so it was not corrected after the last occurrence. At home, ask Tara to sort a few examples into observation, hypothesis, law or theory and explain whether each is describing a pattern or explaining why.
